subject: Request: SOC 2 coverage playbook for Dedicated & Private deployments
messages:
From: Jane Smith <jane.smith@acmecorp.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 applicability for Dedicated / VPC — need confirmation and bridge letter

Hi Karthik,

We're preparing for our internal procurement review and need to confirm the scope of Redwood's latest SOC 2 Type II report. Two quick asks:

1) Does the current SOC 2 Type II coverage extend to Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) that we would lease in our account, or do Dedicated pools require a separate attestation / bridge letter?
2) For Private/VPC or on-prem packages, what evidence (if any) can Redwood provide — is a bridge letter sufficient or do you require a scoped SOC 2 addendum?

Our compliance deadline is May 8; if you can point us to a short checklist or an official bridge letter template that clarifies audit period and deployment applicability, that would help speed sign-off.

Thanks,
Jane Smith
Senior Security Manager
Acme Corp
security@acmecorp.com

--
Attachment: (none in this message)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Smith <jane.smith@acmecorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 applicability for Dedicated / VPC — need confirmation and bridge letter

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front, followed by an action plan: 

- Hosted (multi-tenant Redwood API): covered by our existing SOC 2 Type II report (same audit period noted in the summary).
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): generally covered under our SOC 2 report when customers are hosted on Redwood-managed Dedicated pools; however, there are edge cases where tenant isolation or customer-managed networking (VPC peering) changes the scope. In those cases we provide a bridge letter that clarifies which controls are still applicable and any customer responsibilities.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: typically not in-scope for the standard SOC 2; we produce a bridge letter and a deployment-specific responsibility matrix. For on-prem installs we typically provide an evidence package and an integration checklist rather than adding the environment to our standard Type II.

I've attached a short one-page summary that maps deployment modes to typical SOC 2 treatment and the audit-period language we use (Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf). Next steps I propose:

1) I'll loop in Marissa (Legal/Compliance) and Ben (Customer Success) to draft a bridge letter tailored to Acme's required audit period.
2) If you can share the specific audit window you need covered (start/end dates) and whether you'll be using Dedicated pools managed by Redwood or deploying a VPC/on-prem package, we can produce the appropriate document within 3 business days.

Would you prefer a templated bridge letter first or a short playbook/checklist that your procurement team can review?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf (summary mapping, 1 page)
